name: Worcester Woods Country Park Orchard
description: Hornhill Orchard within Worcester Woods Country Park features heritage apple, pear and damson trees planted on ancient meadow. A Meadow Trail self-guided walk passes through the orchard; fruit is open to public foraging in small quantities under the council's foraging policy.

name: Trotshill Community Orchard
description: A volunteer-restored orchard within Trotshill Copse, planted around 20 years ago as part of the Warndon Villages housing development. Trees are now in full production. Practical working sessions on the 3rd Saturday of each month; public foraging of windfalls encouraged.

name: Cherry Orchard Local Nature Reserve
short_description: Historic cherry and fruit trees on south Worcester slopes.
description: A Local Nature Reserve on the southern slopes of Worcester with old cherry, plum and apple trees among species-rich grassland. Worcester City Council permits small-quantity foraging of fruit in accordance with its Fruit Picking and Foraging Policy.

name: Gorse Hill and Elbury Mount LNR
short_description: Scrub and bramble on Worcester's highest point.
description: The highest point in Worcester City, with footpaths winding through mature oaks, scrub and bramble. Hawthorn haws, blackberries and rosehips are abundant along the wooded edges and open scrub in late summer and autumn.

name: Laugherne Brook LNR Watercress & Wild Greens
short_description: Brook-side wild watercress and meadow herbs.
description: The damp bankside of Laugherne Brook supports watercress beds, wild watermint and wood sorrel. Access via footpaths alongside the brook. Forage lightly in accordance with Worcester City Council's policy.

name: Perry Wood Wild Garlic and Hazelnuts
short_description: Ancient woodland spring garlic and autumn nuts.
description: Perry Wood Local Nature Reserve is a remnant of ancient semi-natural woodland. Carpets of wild garlic appear in spring, while hazel coppice produces hazelnuts in autumn. A popular and accessible foraging wood close to the city centre.

name: Offerton Lane LNR Sloes and Elder
short_description: Hedgerow harvest along the Offerton Lane reserve.
description: A small Local Nature Reserve with dense hedgerow featuring blackthorn (sloes), elder, and crab apple. The elder provides flowers in early summer and berries in autumn; sloes are best gathered after the first frost.

name: Westbury Street Community Garden
short_description: Urban community growing beds in St John's.
description: A small community garden in the St John's neighbourhood managed by local volunteers, growing seasonal vegetables, culinary herbs and soft fruit available for community harvest. Beds include kale, chard, courgettes and climbing beans through summer.

name: Ronkswood Hill Meadows Rosehips and Haws
short_description: Hedgerow fruit along the Ronkswood hill perimeter.
description: Hedgerow species around the Ronkswood Hill Meadows nature reserve provide good rosehip and hawthorn haw crops from late summer. The wilder boundary scrub also has scattered elder and occasional sloe.

name: Warndon Wood Wild Garlic and Blackberries
short_description: Damp woodland garlic and summer berry picking.
description: Warndon Wood Local Nature Reserve is a secluded patch of semi-natural woodland with wild garlic in spring and substantial blackberry growth along sunny woodland edges in late summer. Quiet and lightly visited.

name: Lyppard Grange LNR Blackberries
short_description: Bramble and scrub berry picking in east Worcester.
description: The scrubby fringes and open grassland edges of Lyppard Grange Local Nature Reserve carry dense bramble producing good blackberry crops through August and September.

name: Ombersley Community Orchard
short_description: Heritage orchard behind the Crown and Sandys village.
description: A 0.8 hectare orchard planted between 1998 and 2001 with 64 fruit trees — apple, pear, plum, damson, cherry, walnut and mulberry — on a former grazing field behind the Crown and Sandys Hotel. Community foraging is welcomed.

name: Tolladine Wood Wild Greens
short_description: Shaded woodland edge herbs and spring greens.
description: The woodland margins of Tolladine Wood Local Nature Reserve support seasonal wild foods including wood sorrel, hawthorn leaf shoots in spring and elderflower along the sunnier boundaries in early summer.

name: Severn Riverside Wild Beet and Samphire
short_description: River bank greens along the Severn floodplain.
description: The damp margins and flood-banks of the River Severn south of the city support wild sea beet and watermint. Accessible via the Severn Way long-distance footpath. Pick lightly following the council foraging guidance.

name: New Plantation LNR Hazelnuts and Sloes
short_description: Young plantation scrub nuts and hedgerow fruit.
description: New Plantation Local Nature Reserve contains mixed young woodland and scrub with hazel coppice producing hazelnuts and scattered blackthorn giving autumn sloes, complemented by rosehip-bearing dog roses along the open edges.
